title: NCBI Bookshelf: Kidney anatomy
scope: Anatomical relationships, coverings, cortex, collecting system and pleural relations. Questions are independently worded; this is an anatomy reference, not a treatment guideline.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Renal artery anatomy
scope: Renal hilar vein–artery–pelvis order, right retrocaval arterial course and segmental functional end arteries; vascular variants require individual imaging.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Renal vein anatomy
scope: Anterior aortomesenteric relationship of the left renal vein and usual gonadal venous drainage.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Horseshoe kidney
scope: Classical inferior mesenteric arterial relationship during ascent; fusion, position and vascular anatomy vary.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Ureter anatomy
scope: Retroperitoneal course, pelvic relationships, adventitial blood supply and intramural antireflux mechanism. Crossing the iliac vessels is a landmark, not necessarily a true anatomical narrowing.

title: EAU Paediatric Urology 2026: Ureterocele and ectopic ureter
scope: Duplex collecting systems, typical upper-pole ureteric insertion and female infrasphincteric ectopic ureter presentation; describes typical relationships, not an exception-free rule.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Bladder anatomy
scope: Trigone, urachal remnant, retropubic space, detrusor and peritoneal relationships.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Prostate anatomy
scope: Prostatic zones, ejaculatory ducts, posterior fascial plane and apical sphincter relations.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Inferior hypogastric plexus anatomy
scope: Autonomic pelvic plexus and cavernous nerve pathways; neurovascular distribution is variable rather than one fixed bundle at every level.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Penis anatomy
scope: Corpora cavernosa and spongiosum, urethral position, tunica albuginea and deep penile fascia.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Male genitourinary tract anatomy
scope: Male urethral regions, bulbourethral duct opening and seminal tract relationships.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Testis anatomy
scope: Testicular lymphatics, venous drainage, pampiniform countercurrent exchange and epididymal continuity.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Scrotal anatomy
scope: Scrotal skin lymphatic drainage distinguished from testicular retroperitoneal drainage.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Testicular embryology
scope: Developmental attachment and bell-clapper predisposition to intravaginal torsion.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Physiology of the bladder
scope: Parasympathetic detrusor contraction and sympathetic storage-phase pathways; segmental levels are approximate physiological ranges.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Pudendal nerve anatomy
scope: Somatic S2–S4 supply to the external urethral sphincter and terminal sensory branches.

title: NCBI Bookshelf: Dorsal penile nerve anatomy
scope: Dorsal penile nerve as a pudendal sensory branch, distinguished from autonomic cavernous nerves.

title: EAU Sexual and Reproductive Health 2026: Priapism
scope: Sections 10.1.2–10.1.3 and Table 10.4: distinguish ischaemic from non-ischaemic priapism; optional early oral terbutaline after intracavernous injection must not delay definitive ischaemia treatment; refractory priapism and MRI evidence of necrosis support counselling about early prosthesis.

title: EAU Renal Cell Carcinoma 2026: Diagnostic evaluation
scope: Sections 5.2.3 and 5.3: sestamibi remains an emerging technique with insufficient external validation; renal mass biopsy can guide selection for surveillance and is required before ablation.

title: EAU Renal Cell Carcinoma 2026: Pathology and oncocytic tumours
scope: Sections 3.5.4–3.5.5: oncocytic biopsy findings are not automatic proof of oncocytoma or benignity; surveillance is an option for appropriately selected patients.

title: EAU Renal Cell Carcinoma 2026: Disease management
scope: Sections 7.2.4.b–d: active surveillance of selected small renal masses, histological risk assessment and biopsy before ablation; surveillance is not limited to proven benign lesions.

title: EAU Prostate Cancer 2026: Diagnostic evaluation
scope: Risk-adapted early detection for BRCA2 carriers and biopsy decisions incorporating MRI, PSA density and individual risk; negative MRI does not exclude clinically significant cancer.

title: S3-Leitlinie Prostatakarzinom, Kurzversion 8.1: Früherkennung und Diagnostik
scope: Recommendations 4.4–4.10: PSA intervals, confirmation of raised PSA and the specific risk clinic/MRI/biopsy pathway for pathogenic BRCA2, MSH2 or MSH6 variants. Version 8.1, published 2025, checked at the current official programme page on 2026-10-11.

title: EMA: Welireg (belzutifan), EU product information
scope: Current EU indication and dose modifications, including interruption and dose reduction after grade 3 hypoxia; not a substitute for a patient-specific prescription.
